newsitem.title: FRANCE: Stabbed French minister concerned about assailant.
newsitem.headline: Stabbed French minister concerned about assailant.

text.p: French Culture Minister Philippe Douste-Blazy, recovering from a stab wound to the lung and two broken ribs, said on Monday he was happy to be alive and was concerned about the mental suffering of his assailant.
"I am happy to be alive," Douste-Blazy said.
"As for my aggressor, I think about his mental suffering," he told reporters in the garden of the hospital where he was being treated for his wounds.

Douste-Blazy was attacked on Friday while on a campaign trip to his constituency in Lourdes, southwestern France, a Catholic shrine known for its healing waters. France is holding a two-round parliamentary election on May 25-June 1.

Doctors said the minister, who is also mayor of Lourdes, would remain in hospital for a few more days and would have to miss this week's inauguration of the Cannes film festival because of his convalescence.
A 37-year-old man of Albanian origin, Adlal Cifti, has been placed under investigation for premeditated attempted murder in connection with the knifing but has denied guilt.
Cifti, who was under psychiatric treatement, attacked Douste-Blazy with a screwdriver in 1992.
"This ordeal has made me even more eager to get out and campaign. I've never been in better shape for winning, and that is why I am eager to leave this hospital," Douste-Blazy said.
